description: Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU), NSF NHERI 2024: Evaluation of Soil Liquefaction Susceptibility in Portland, Oregon: Application of the Direct Push Cross-Hole (DPCH) Method is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Kenneth Stokoe, University of Texas at Austin (utexas.edu). This study evaluates the liquefaction potential of soils at the Sunderland site in Portland, Oregon, using the direct push cross-hole (DPCH) method. By integrating field data and computational analysis, it reveals a low probability of liquefaction due to the cohesive properties of soft clay. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project with 3 top-level files (PDF). Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-yn0w-mg89. Keywords: NSF NHERI Large Mobile Shakers. Published 2024-08-14. Facility named: Mobile Field Shakers - University of Texas at Austin. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
